name: jOlt World Championship
epitaph: jOlt's top belt, first won by Brandon Blade at a2o: Alpha To Omega on 24 June 2001. The fed's own title history carries it through Blade, HaVoK, Blade again and erØn, who left holding it and had it vacated at Rise of the Legends on 28 October 2001, and gives it to The Don at Cataclysm on 30 December. The fed's other accounts also name Kodiak Vic Creed its champion: Unwanted's opening video of 2002 shows him among the past champions, the 2005 site replays the Cataclysm match among its 'jOlt Vintage Classics' and ends it with 'new jOlt World Heavyweight Champion: Kodiak Vic Creed', and its Mardi Gras write-up says the re-make of the belt served 'for Kodiak Vic Creed and The Don’s reigns'. The second season began in May 2002 by putting the belt up again: at Unwanted on 28 May 2002 Erik Rave won a thirty-man battle royale and with it 'a NEW jOlt World Championship'. The revival of 2012 opened with Brandon Blade as the jOlt Champion on iNtense 35; Damien Lee fired him on iNtense 36, and the belt was contested at Divide & Conquer, whose first review is dated 30 July 2012: Sylo beat Superstar Vince Jacobs there for it, in a main event that also ended the Legacy title. Derecho won it at Power Struggle in June 2013 and lost it to Aran Thompson at Thieves' Honor that August; Jeremy Ryan was its champion in 2015, and Death Wish, the final show, books him against Omega in a steel cage for it and the Fearless belt.

name: jOlt International Championship
epitaph: The belt Erik Rave won at iNtense 10, which passed to Bane Loneheart, Azrael Ravenell, Reno Davis, who vacated it the night he won it at Thieves Honour, and Rush before Azrael Ravenell took it again at Rise of the Legends on 28 October 2001. He defended it into 2002; J-Con won the title from Trey Vincent by submission at Unwanted on 28 May 2002. The revival of 2012 opened with Rush as its champion; Jonathan Conspiracy beat him for it on Warriors 02, whose first review is dated 28 June 2012, and lost it to The Nashvillain at Divide & Conquer, where it was absorbed into the Relentless title.

name: jOlt World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Total Conquest, Sepiroth Du Luc and Persephone, won the vacant belts at iNtense 22 and lost them at Thieves Honour to Fueled by V.I.A.G.R.A., who lost them at Rise of the Legends to V.I.A.G.R.A., High Flyer and Tony Davis. Chris Titan and Mike Extreme won them at Cataclysm by the fed's own title history; Team V.I.A.G.R.A. took them back on 3 February 2002, and Derecho and Blazer won them in the Tag Team Turmoil Gauntlet at Unwanted on 28 May 2002. In the 2012 revival the Heirs of Wrestling won the belts in a four-corners match at Divide & Conquer and kept them against Sylo and Ray Chavez on Warriors 05.

name: jOlt X-Treme Championship
epitaph: Graphic Violence won the vacant belt at Rise of the Legends on 28 October 2001 and vacated it at Cataclysm on 30 December, where KroW won it from the Extremist. The card of 20 January 2002 still calls KroW 'the X-Treme champion'.

name: Moral Championship
epitaph: LLB's own belt: he wore a 'Morally the jOlt World Champion' shirt on 16 December 2001, and the card of 20 January 2002 shows him defending the Moral Title, which Wippit Guud calls not a real jOlt title. He retained it in a ladder match against Wippit Guud on 3 February 2002.

name: Revolutionary Championship
epitaph: Created for jOlt's second season: Dave Gibson won the first Revolutionary Championship at Unwanted on 28 May 2002 when the referee disqualified Sam Potright for a foreign object.

name: Jolt Ambassador Championship
epitaph: The 2005 site's second belt ('The 2nd belt in this company'), to be defended at least every thirty days and carried by its champion as Jolt's ambassador whenever another federation asked for a wrestler. Kenjiro Ito won it at WrestleSault I on 27 February 2005, beating Chris Mezz in the match the pay-per-view gave the Triple Crown semi-finals' runners-up, and took it outside Jolt within three weeks, beating Aimz on PRIME Wrestling's ReVolution 58 of 16 March; the night before, his main-event defence against Carson Nash had ended in a no contest.
notes: The rules: the 2005 information page (/promotions/jolt-2001/archive/jolt-2001-information-faq-2005.html). The title match: the site's own WrestleSault I review (/promotions/jolt-2001/archive/jolt-2001-column-6-2005-03-01.html).

name: Jolt Triple Crown Championship
epitaph: The 2005 site's top singles prize: three belts, the 2001 jOlt World Heavyweight Title, the 2002 jOlt World Championship and the new Triple Crown Title, decided by a tournament through February 2005. Brandon Youngblood won its final from Jeff Garvin at WrestleSault I on 27 February after fifty-four minutes; on the 15 March Tuesday Night Intense he threw the belt down to save Melissa Garvin from Garvin's Hammer Jammer, and the page ends asking whether he had forfeited it. Kenjiro Ito's own later biography cards say he won it on Jolt's last show.
notes: Sources disagree on the last champion: Kenjiro Ito's PRIME card (/promotions/prime-2003/archive/kenjiro-ito-bio.html) and GCW card (/promotions/gcw-gcwonline-2001/archive/kenjiro-ito-bio.html) name him; fWo's own text of 21 September 2005 (/promotions/fwo-fans-1998/archive/fwo-fans-1998-disney-s-wednesday-warfare-2005-09-21.html) bills Carson Nash 'the last Jolt Triple Crown Champion'.

name: Relentless Championship
epitaph: The Nashvillain was the Relentless Champion when the revival opened and kept the belt against Jonathan Conspiracy on iNtense 35; the board's reviews note that the champion cannot turn down a match. Reno Davis took it from him on Warriors 05, and at Divide & Conquer the review says the International title was absorbed into it.

name: Underground Championship
epitaph: Derecho was the Underground Champion when the revival opened. He defended it against Rune Winters on iNtense 35 and BIG Little Italy on Warriors 01 and met Citizen for it at Divide & Conquer; the board's reviews call him its champion through iNtense 38.

name: Flyweight Championship
epitaph: Avispa Ultima was the Flyweight Champion on Warriors 01, where he faced Sanchez Cano and Cordova; a member asks in the review whether the belt is to be called the LoC Flyweight Championship.
